health.notice_text: Passyble works out each password's SHA-1 fingerprint on this device and sends only its first 5 characters to Have I Been Pwned (api.pwnedpasswords.com, run by Troy Hunt). The answers are padded, so their size reveals nothing. Passyble never sends a password, a full hash, an e-mail address, a username or a website. Like any website, Have I Been Pwned can see this device's IP address.

settings.auto_lock_info: How soon Passyble locks by itself. With a time chosen, filling, copying or auto-typing a login, a 2FA code or a card, a passkey sign-in and working in this window start the time again, up to the time chosen here; pages the browser opens in the background don't. With a time, or "When the computer locks or sleeps", Passyble also locks on Win+L and when the PC sleeps. "On every restart" keeps it unlocked until Passyble or the PC restarts. Locking forgets the vault key.

settings.keep_list_info: Locking keeps your list on screen without passwords or 2FA codes: auto-lock, Lock (Ctrl+L, the lock button, the tray), Win+L, sleep, and also after quitting or restarting Passyble. Passyble asks to unlock only when you copy, show or change something. The vault key is forgotten either way. The list (titles, usernames and websites, never passwords) is also kept on this PC, encrypted for your Windows account, so the browser extension shows your logins right after Passyble starts; picking one unlocks first. Off: locking hides everything, and the kept list is deleted. Only "Lock completely" (Ctrl+Shift+L, the lock button's menu or the tray menu) also hides the list until you unlock, and deletes the kept copy.
settings.confirm_each_fill_info: Even while unlocked, ask for Windows Hello before the extension fills a login, 2FA code or passkey, and before auto-type.
settings.after_confirming_info: After Windows Hello, fills don't ask again for this long. Each fill, copy or passkey sign-in in that time starts it again, up to the time chosen here; once it runs out, the next fill asks. With Every time, each login fill asks (unlocking for that login counts once); only the 2FA code of the login you just confirmed fills without asking, for 2 minutes.

help.totp_2: In Passyble, edit the site's login and paste the key into {field}. Passyble shows the current code so you can check it.
help.totp_3: Type that code on the site to finish. From then on, the browser extension fills the code on the step after the password.
help.totp_4: In the browser extension's own editor, Scan QR on this page reads the QR code for you.
help.totp_5: In other apps, copy the code from the login in Passyble, or use the small code window that opens after auto-type.

help.passkeys_1: With the browser extension, when a site offers to create a passkey, Passyble saves it in your vault after asking you.
help.passkeys_2: Next time, choose to sign in with a passkey: Passyble uses the one it saved, no password needed.
help.passkeys_3: If Passyble has no passkey for the site, isn't running or stays locked, the browser's own passkey dialog opens instead.
help.passkeys_4: On an up-to-date Windows 11, turn on {path} so that other apps, and browsers without the extension, can use your Passyble passkeys too.
help.passkeys_note: Passkeys are part of your vault: they sync and are backed up with it.
help.sync_title: Sync with your phone and other PCs
help.sync_intro: Your vault is one encrypted file. Keep a copy on each device in one of these ways:
help.sync_server: Passyble Server (run by your organization or family): for the vault that is already open, use {path}. On a new device, choose {signin} on the welcome screen and use the same account.
help.sync_google: Google Drive: turn on {path}. On another PC, choose {restore} when you add the vault.
help.sync_folder: OneDrive or Dropbox folder (PCs only): move the vault file into it with {path}. On the other PC, choose {open}.
help.sync_webdav: WebDAV (Nextcloud and others): enter the file's address under {path}. On the other device, choose {restore} under {more}.
help.sync_phone: On a phone, the Passyble Android app connects the same way: Passyble Server or WebDAV.
help.sync_install: To use Passyble on another PC, install it from the downloads page first.
help.sync_note: Only the encrypted vault leaves this PC. Your master password stays the key, on every device.
help.import_1: In your old password manager or browser, export your passwords to a file. The Import page explains how for each app.
help.import_2: Open Import and choose the export file, or drop it on the Passyble window.
help.import_3: Check the preview: entries for the same account are merged, and where the passwords differ you pick the one to keep. Then import.
help.import_4: Delete the export file afterwards: it holds your passwords unencrypted.
help.recovery_title: Recovery code and a forgotten master password
help.recovery_1: Only you know your master password. Nobody can reset it for you, not even Sensyble.
help.recovery_2: A recovery code is your way back in. Create one in {path}, then print it or save it somewhere safe, away from this PC.
help.recovery_3: Forgot your master password? On the unlock screen, choose {forgot}, enter the code and pick a new master password.
help.recovery_4: On a Passyble Server vault the master password is your server password: the code unlocks the vault, and the new password comes from the server's reset ({forgot} on the sign-in form) or from your admin.
help.recovery_note: Keep the code secret: like your master password, it opens your vault.

aitools.title: AI tools
aitools.how_it_works: The Passyble connector for AI tools lets Claude Code, Codex and other MCP clients run commands with secrets from the items you share, without the AI seeing them. You approve each use here in Passyble, which shows the exact command. Secret values in the command's output are hidden, but a command can still send a secret wherever it connects to, so read the command before you allow it.

aitools.not_installed_info: The connector isn't beside Passyble. Reinstall Passyble to get it.
aitools.appimage: The AppImage runs from a new folder each time, so there is no fixed path for AI tools yet. Use the .deb or .rpm package for AI tools.
aitools.claude_code_note: Run this in a terminal. --scope user makes it available in all your projects; leave it out for the current project only.
aitools.codex_note: Add this to ~/.codex/config.toml. Codex gives a tool call 60 seconds by default, too short to answer the approval prompt.
